value.Name: Rhody F1rst (URI STUDENT SENATE)
value.Description:
Rhody F1rst is a student-led organization dedicated to supporting, empowering, and celebrating first-generation college students. As the university’s first organization created by and for first-gen students, Rhody F1rst offers a unique and comprehensive support system that significantly benefits the URI community.


Rhody F1rst provides a vibrant community where first-generation students can connect, share experiences, and thrive together. The organization offers mentorship opportunities, allowing students to receive guidance from peers who understand their unique challenges and experiences. This peer support system fosters a sense of belonging and helps students navigate the college experience with confidence.


The organization organizes workshops and social events that focus on various aspects of student life, including academic success, financial literacy, and career planning. These events provide first-gen students with valuable information and resources to help them succeed academically and professionally. Additionally, Rhody F1rst collaborates with campus departments to ensure students have access to essential resources and support services.


Rhody F1rst serves as a voice for first-generation students within the URI community. The organization advocates for policies and initiatives that address the unique needs of first-gen students, ensuring they have equal opportunities to succeed. By raising awareness and promoting inclusivity, Rhody F1rst contributes to a more equitable and supportive campus environment.
Through its various programs and events, Rhody F1rst fosters a strong sense of community among first-generation students. The organization encourages students to engage with one another, build lasting relationships, and support each other throughout their college journey. This sense of community not only enhances the student experience but also contributes to higher retention and graduation rates among first-gen students.


Therefore, Rhody F1rst uniquely benefits the URI community by providing first-generation students with the support, resources, and advocacy they need to succeed. Through its peer mentorship, workshops, and community-building efforts, the organization plays a crucial role in fostering an inclusive and supportive environment at URI.

* This organization is open to all enrolled undergraduates in good standing at URI.
value.Summary:
Rhody F1rst is a supportive community for first-generation college students, offering guidance, resources, and connection.

value.Name: Supply Chain Management Club
value.Description:
The Supply Chain Management Club creates a community among students who are interested in the evolving dynamics of supply chain within the business world. Each semester we find new opportunities to get out of the classroom and immerse ourselves in:

  • Networking Events – to start conversations with dozens of Supply Chain professionals
  • Company Presentations – to hear from real companies and the challenges they face every day
  • Alumni Panels – to understand different experiences that recent graduates have had during their transition to the workforce
  • Field Trips – to experience the business environment first-hand and be able to ask questions on the spot
  • Job & Internship Opportunities – are continuously shared amongst the club with connections from professionals looking for URI graduates.

We encourage any student who is interested in the various career paths of supply chain to join: planning, forecasting, category management, transportation, logistics, warehousing, operations, network design, process improvement, production, purchasing, marketing, customer relations, supplier relations, omni-channel fulfillment, big data, etc. Learn more about the club with these helpful links

value.Name: URI Alpine (URI STUDENT SENATE)
value.Description:
Who we are:
We are the URI Ski Team! We offer an opportunity to ski or snowboard at an intermediate+ level. If you like going fast and enjoy winter thrills, the URI Alpine Team is the club for you!

URI Alpine is a racing team, so you will be competing, but its only as competitive as you make it. Some skiers with more experience are aiming for medals. Other team members set personal goals or have friendly rivalries with other racers with similar skill levels. 


What the Season Looks Like:
During winter break, we do our yearly training camp to give everyone an opportunity to get a few runs in before the season as well as ski gates. For many of our new recruits, this will be there first experience with a race course.

Including the training camp, we go on a total of 5 ski trips. Meaning every weekend for 5 weeks, we carpool after Friday classes, stay in an Airbnb till Sunday, and are home Sunday evening for dinner.

In Alpine racing there are two disciplines that we race, Slalom and Giant Slalom (GS). On Saturdays we compete in a slalom race and on Sunday we compete in a GS race. There are also opportunities during the season to do park events called Rail Jam.

Ability Threshold and Equipment:
We recommend that you are a good enough skier/boarder to confidently ski/board blue trails.

You will need to supply your own ski equipment for the season, including a hard-eared helmet, skis/board, boots, and poles if your a skier.

* This organization is open to all enrolled undergraduates in good standing at URI.

Currently, we have Counter Strike 2, Fortnite, Rocket League, and Minecraft approved for installation on the computers. Our next goal is to get Overwatch, Rainbow 6 Siege, Valorant, League of Legends, Call of Duty, and Apex Legends approved to provide more students with opportunities to practice and play in a LAN environment.

 

We hold tryouts for official rosters each semester. Instead of recurring meetings, we have team rosters that practice and compete weekly, participate in LAN tournaments, and offer regular activities such as Minecraft Bed Wars and club outings, all of which are open to any member. Please join our Discord server for more information.

value.Name: Graduate Student Association
value.Description:
The Graduate Student Association (GSA) is a government body maintained by and for the graduate students of the University with the purpose of enhancing the academic, intellectual, and social opportunities of its members. Officers and members of the GSA Senate, elected annually from the entire graduate student body, distribute GSA funds to graduate students and other qualifying groups, organize social events, and serve as graduate student representatives on University-wide committees.

Every graduate student at URI donates to the funds of the GSA through the student activities fee. All GSA programs; events; activities; and decisions are managed by the GSA executive committee as mandated by the GSA Constitution. The executive board is composed of a president; vice-president; secretary; treasurer; and a representative at large, who acts as the webmaster for the GSA website. Each board member is responsible for the duties of their respective position. Each executive board member is elected on an annual basis by voting members of the senate. GSA senators attend monthly meetings with the executive board to discuss and vote on GSA policy decisions. Executive board members have no voting privileges. Any graduate student may sign up to be a GSA senator; for every 20 graduate students, a graduate department is entitled to one department senator. All GSA policy, constitution, and by-law decisions are made by the voting senators. All board members and senators are paid for their duties and contributions to the GSA.
value.Summary: The Graduate Student Association (GSA) is a government body maintained by and for the graduate students of the University with the purpose of enhancing the academic, intellectual, and social opportunities of its members.

value.Name: Talent Development
value.Description:
Following the assassination of Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr., the University of Rhode Island (URI) established Talent Development (TD) as a special admission program for Rhode Island students, primarily those from under-performing schools. From that first class of 13 students in ’68 to the 1,000 current Scholars and nearly 5,000 alumni, TD is a proud community of accomplished individuals in this state, across the country, and worldwide.

 

Talent Development recruits and serves high school graduates from Rhode Island with college potential, most of whom come from under-performing schools.

 

Talent Development’s core values are grounded in the University’s mission of enriching students’ lives through its land, sea, and urban grant traditions. This is reflected in our ongoing commitment to Respect, Academic Excellence, Mental Health & Wellness, and Scholar Success. We are invested in cultivating the intellectual, social, and cultural development of our Scholars. We inspire Scholars to discover, create, and innovate while fostering leadership and personal growth to build a foundation for persistence.

 

Follow us @TDNation68 on Instagram!

value.Name: Timmy Global Health (URI STUDENT SENATE)
value.Description:
Vision:
Building a healthier world through a community of global leaders.

Mission:
Timmy Global Health works to empower communities to address health disparities in a sustainable way. By empower, we mean more than involvement, participation, or engagement – this implies ownership. Through increased capacity, we strive for communities to take ownership of the health initiatives that address health disparities in a sustainable way.

What We Do at URI
At the University of Rhode Island, our multi-cultural chapter advances this mission through service, advocacy, and fundraising on campus, in the local community, and internationally. We focus on supporting rural communities where access to essential health services is limited.

We currently partner with communities in the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, and Nigeria, addressing critical health challenges including:

Access to care
Maternal and child health
Nutrition
Water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH)

What You Can Expect as a Member
Service
Participate in at least 4 volunteer events each year focused on health and wellness needs within our campus and surrounding communities.

📣 Advocacy
Join us for 4 or more advocacy events aimed at raising awareness of pressing health issues. These events include opportunities for reflection, education, and action.

Fundraising
Help us meet our annual goal of $1,000, which supports our international partners through medical supplies, referral fees, access to care, and targeted programs in maternal health, nutrition, and WASH. Additional fundraising supports medical service trips abroad.

Global Engagement Opportunities
Each year, students may have the opportunity to participate in medical service trips abroad with Timmy Global Health. These trips are open to all (not limited to health majors or clinicians) and may include:
-URI students
-Spanish interpreters
-General volunteers (Friends and family members included for service trips through Timmy HQ)

We also share information about last-minute openings on service brigades throughout the year.

Leadership and Professional Development
We are actively recruiting new members and chair positions. By joining, you’ll gain valuable experience in service and leadership that will:

-Strengthen your CV
-Fulfill PharmD CORE ELMS requirements in both service and leadership categories
-Connect you with a global health network working toward sustainable change

Guided by Timmy’s Core Values
Community-Centered: Listening to and honoring the needs and cultures of the communities we serve

*Capacity-Building: Supporting sustainable solutions and local ownership
*Impact-Driven: Combining empathy with evidence-based programs
*Global Engagement: Connecting students with a worldwide network working for health equity

Ready to Make a Difference?
If you're passionate about global health, committed to equity, or looking for a meaningful way to serve, we invite you to get involved.

We are always open to new members at any time, and are open to collaborating with other organizations in meaningful, impactful ways. Please contact us (via email) if you are interested in any of the opportunities we can offer or connect you to!

Welcome to Fellowships@URI! Our office advises qualified undergraduates, recent URI alumni, and current graduate students on how to explore, apply for, and secure fellowship funding. We are excited to work with you on this journey of reflection and career-preparation as you consider some of the most transformative opportunities locally, nationally, and internationally.

What is a ‘fellowship’? Unlike a scholarship which covers tuition or direct educational costs, fellowships offer a cost-of-living stipend, an internship, a research experience, a study abroad program, or another experiential opportunity. There are fellowships in all fields and for undergraduates, graduates, and alumni alike, but eligibility requirements vary!
value.Summary: Welcome to Fellowships@URI! Our office advises qualified undergraduates, recent URI alumni, and current graduate students on how to explore, apply for, and secure fellowship funding.

value.Name: Office of New Student Transitions
value.Description:
Our goal is to keep you engaged with fun activities as you wait for your first week of classes to begin. This will allow you to be social in a safe way while learning about living on campus.

 

Registration

  • To register for an event, please sign in to URInvolved: urinvolved.uri.edu and create a profile using your Single Sign On (SSO).
  • Once you have signed up for URInvolved, you can access all O-Week Events by clicking the Events tab at the top left of the page.
  • To register for an event, click into the event, and RSVP by clicking and submitting “I will be attending.“
  • Each event is first-come, first-served; however, many events are repeated throughout the week to allow students who move in later the opportunity to participate. 
  • Space for events is limited. If you wish to cancel an event or change your time, open the event, and update your RSVP to “I won’t be attending.”
    Changing your RSVP will allow other students to participate.

Expectations

  • Please arrive 15 minutes early to all events to allow time for check-in, unless more time is specified. For events that provide transportation to and from, it is the students’ responsibility to be at their meeting locations early to ensure buses depart on schedule.

value.Description: Tau Sigma National Honor Society – Iota Nu Chapter at the University of Rhode Island is the national honor society for transfer students, proudly supported by the Fannon Institute for Student Success. The chapter honors transfer students who earn a 3.5 GPA or higher in their first semester at URI and creates a community where their accomplishments are recognized and celebrated. Beyond recognition, Tau Sigma provides members with opportunities to take on leadership roles, participate in community service, engage in professional development, and connect with other transfer students who share similar experiences. Through annual induction ceremonies, social events, and strong advisor support, the Iota Nu Chapter helps transfer students feel connected, supported, and valued at URI while also linking them to a national network of Tau Sigma chapters across the country.
